theorem u5_qcritical_gramcert_pattern_incompatibility

Gate-facing incompatibility for the sweep predicate `qcritical_gramcert`:
a q-critical residual pattern on which the Gram-certificate checker fires
is unrealizable by any configuration.

The hypotheses are exactly the facts every residual row supplies (the
same surface as `u5_qcritical_propagation_pattern_incompatibility`): the
dangerous triple, the per-row witnesses at the labelled centers, the
membership transfer from the encoded pattern to the row classes, and the
checker certificate.

display_text:
# Phase-0d Gram-certificate checker — facts and verifier

The fact-polynomial table and the Boolean certificate verifier for the U5
Phase-0d Gram-certificate checker
(`docs/u-lane/97-u5-grampair-phase0d-checker-design-2026-06-03.md` §2.2).

Polynomial variables index the norms and pairwise inner products of the
vectors from `p` of the 8 labelled points (`u5VarIdx`): the unordered pair
`{a, b}` gets index `8 * min + max`, so norms sit on the diagonal
(`u5VarIdx a a = 9 * a`).  Pairs involving `p = 0` evaluate to `0` under
the realization assignment, so the fact builders need no special-casing.

The fact table of a pattern `P` (`u5GramFacts`):

* 3 base facts `N_q − N_{tᵢ}` (the p-circle);
* per row, for each member pair `z₁, z₂` (sorted order), the row-pair fact
  `(N_{z₁} − 2·D_{c,z₁}) − (N_{z₂} − 2·D_{c,z₂})` (row equidistance with
  the center norm cancelled);
* the 35 planar Gram-determinant facts over triples of non-`p` points.

A certificate (`U5GramCertificate`) is a list of `(fact index, cofactor)`
pairs plus a target polynomial `m`.  The checker
(`u5GramCertChecker`) accepts when `Σ cᵢ·fᵢ − m` passes the zero test and
`m` meets the positivity criterion: all collected coefficients
nonnegative, support on norm variables only (`u5NormVar`), and at least
one positive collected coefficient on a monomial supported on the
strictly-positive-available norms (`u5GramStrictVar`).

The checker is **never kernel-evaluated inside Lean** — the Python sweep
mirrors it term by term; Lean supplies the soundness theorem
(`U5GramCertSound.lean`).
